analytical_question: As of 2026-10-13, America/New_York, should this hypothetical conservative delivery fleet proceed with a grid-export trial while preserving charge for daily routes?
general_et_finding: V2G requires export-capable vehicles, compatible equipment, and utility interconnection permission; V2B backup and ordinary managed charging are distinct uses. DOE describes limited diffusion of vehicle grid-service incentive programs, not universal technical or commercial readiness.
application_finding: For this application, export capability alone does not establish suitability: dispatch controls must preserve route energy and permit human interruption. Ordinary managed charging is the strongest alternative to evaluate because it addresses charging needs without deliberately exporting energy needed for deliveries.
organization_specific_finding: Written pilot permission and compatible trial hardware are hypothetical inputs, not verified fleet facts. The decisive blocker is the organization's explicit refusal to expose route vehicles before warranty and commercial terms are documented; conservative appetite does not change the general technology evidence.

evidence.claim: DOE distinguishes managed charging, V2B, and V2G; it identifies compatible bidirectional equipment and utility reverse-power permission as relevant conditions.
evidence.source_or_reference: U.S. Department of Energy, Managed and Bidirectional Charging: https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging
evidence.date_or_recency: Page undated; supplied packet records retrieval on 2026-10-13.
evidence.evidence_type: Primary-source guidance; supplied dated evidence packet, corroborated by live page.
evidence.notes: DOE also describes limited availability of vehicle grid-service incentive programs. No fleet-specific authorization, warranty coverage, or savings follows from this guidance. ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))

evidence.claim: The fleet has written pilot permission and compatible trial hardware but will not expose route vehicles until warranty and commercial terms are documented.
evidence.evidence_type: Hypothetical input assumptions, not external observations.
evidence.notes: These assumptions support preparation, not an inference that missing coverage or liability terms have been accepted.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Counter-case: documented acceptable terms and demonstrated route-reserve controls could support a bounded export experiment, but not routine adoption.
The undated DOE page does not establish fleet-scale maturity; its exact historical contents on 2026-10-13 cannot be independently authenticated here. Later developments are excluded.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in deferral under the stated organizational constraint; low confidence in eventual economics or operational suitability. This is a teaching-case judgment, not field deployment evidence.
value_opportunity_implication: Deferral preserves an option to learn without committing delivery capacity. Evaluate managed charging as the baseline; incremental grid-export value remains unproven until compensation, costs, and vehicle-use terms are documented.
risk_governance_implication: Unexpected discharge could interrupt a delivery under the case assumptions. Before export, require documented warranty coverage and liability allocation, plus demonstrated reserve enforcement and human stop authority; missing terms are not accepted risks.
recommendation_management_implication: Defer operational grid export. Immediately permit document review and a non-export proof of concept using simulation or isolated equipment without exposing route vehicles; pass operating-capacity assessment and implementation ownership to the Organizational Adoption Agent.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reconsider for a bounded experiment when acceptable warranty and commercial terms are documented and route-reserve controls pass a non-export demonstration.
If preparation reveals unreliable reserve enforcement or permission that excludes the proposed operation, retain deferral and reassess feasibility.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Obtain manufacturer warranty language and proposed commercial terms covering export, compensation, battery-related responsibility, and liability.
Confirm that the assumed written permission covers the specific trial configuration; abstain from judging savings or routine-adoption readiness without fleet-specific evidence.
